name: NEUMANN, the Hon. Shayne Kenneth

headline.note: Official records establish private legal practice from 1985 to the 2007 election, and first-person material identifies Neumann and Turnour Lawyers, partnership, family-law specialization and 1996 accreditation. They do not publish hours, leave, exact partnership commencement, other early legal employers or cessation day. His student meatworks job was part-time; party, governance and elected roles are excluded. No full-time public/private total is therefore calculated. Articled-clerk work from1983 is separately supported but employer, cessation and hours remain unknown. Election date is not used as a legal-practice cessation day.

career_spells.evidence_note: In his first speech Neumann described a part-time cleaner job at Dinmore Meatworks while studying at university. The operator, dates, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Explicitly part-time work is outside the substantive full-time headline measure.

career_spells.role: Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Laws student
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biographies and Neumann's first speech identify arts and law study at UQ, including government and economics majors, without attendance or completion dates.

career_spells.employer: Private legal practice, including Neumann and Turnour Lawyers
career_spells.role: Lawyer; partner and senior partner; accredited family law specialist from 1996
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography gives lawyer from 1985 to 2007. Neumann says he entered business at age 26 as partner in his own firm with Matthew Turnour and built Neumann and Turnour Lawyers in Brisbane; his member profile calls him a senior partner and says he practised about 25 years. Parliamentary speeches establish family-law accreditation in 1996. The Australian Business Register records NEUMANN & TURNOUR LAWYERS as a trading name of The Ezra No 2 Unit Trust from 10 September 2007; this identifies a registered operating name near the end of the interval, not Neumann's personal payroll, partnership start or cessation. Sources do not establish any 1985-to-partnership employer, exact firm start, hours, leave or precise cessation beyond election to Parliament. Follow-up2026-10-02: replaced election-day cessation with official year2007 because no source establishes last working day. Separate1983articled-clerk work below precedes the official1985lawyer interval. Age26partnership and aggregate business-years claims do not justify precise firm-start dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private practice is clear, but an aggregate occupation interval and senior title do not establish continuous full-time service or resolve the early-employer boundary.

career_spells.evidence_note: Neumann's member biography identifies board service. In 2008 parliamentary speeches he said he served for 14 years and ceased before entering the House, but exact appointment/cessation, remuneration and time commitment are not stated. Fourteen years is reported duration, not a dated appointment; no start year derived by subtraction.
career_spells.counting_note: Board governance is excluded from substantive employment totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Member and ABC profiles report service on the local health council before Parliament. Appointment/cessation, remuneration and time commitment are not published. Follow-up: removed assumed2007cessation; source only places service before Parliament. First speech describes nearly a decade without precise boundaries. Public advisory governance is distinct from an established public-service job.

career_spells.role: Raceview Flinders Branch president; Ipswich State Electorate Council president; state and national conference delegate; rules and administrative committee member
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists overlapping internal party positions: branch president from 1990; electorate-council president 1995–2008; state conference delegate 2000–08; rules committee 2002–08; national conference delegate 2004–07 and 2023; administrative committee 2005–08 and from 2022. Paid status, hours and several end dates are unspecified.
The official biography lists this campaign-director interval but does not establish paid status, hours, exact dates or overlap with legal practice.
Official records show election to the House of Representatives for Blair on 24 November 2007 and continuous service thereafter.

career_spells.role: Junior articled law clerk, including family-law work
career_spells.evidence_note: Explicit first-person1983commencement as articled clerk.2010speech recalls conveyancing work in Ipswich, but does not name firm. No inferred1985end, admission day, hours or leave; possible overlap with study/otherwork unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

career_spells.employer: Ipswich family-relationship grandparents reference group; hosting body not established
career_spells.evidence_note: 2010speech describes participation during first parliamentary term in group considering grandparents’ rights. Not recorded as paid employment; later planned participation is not treated as an accomplished appointment.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

sources.title: Historical details for ABN 11 955 351 885
sources.note: Government register records The Ezra No 2 Unit Trust as the entity name from 19 March 2002 to 10 September 2007 and NEUMANN & TURNOUR LAWYERS as a trading name from 10 September 2007. The ABN was active from 1 May 2000; entity dates are not personal employment dates.

research_notes: Identify the Dinmore meatworks operator, dates, hours and leave; work is expressly part-time and remains excluded.
Obtain Queensland admission and legal-practice records identifying every 1985–2007 employer, exact Neumann and Turnour partnership/start/cessation boundaries, hours and leave.
Confirm whether the 1985 lawyer start predates Neumann and Turnour establishment at age 26 and identify any intervening practice.
Obtain appointment/cessation, remuneration and time-commitment records for Queensland Baptist Care and West Moreton District Health Council governance.
Confirm paid status and exact dates for ALP internal and campaign roles; these remain excluded regardless.

Follow-up2026-10-02: revisited parliamentary family-law and first speeches, discovering1983clerkship omitted from original record;2010speech confirms Ipswich conveyance and reference-group participation. Added distinct clerkship and removed unsupported day-level legal cessation and assumed2007health-council cessation.

Targeted firm-history,1983clerk employer,1985lawyer employer, Baptist board and West Moreton council searches did not identify exact appointments or hours. Neumann and Turnour employer website returned (400) Timeout fetching; indexed practice pages did not establish history. Current firm staff and partner admission dates are not Neumann’s employment boundaries.

Dinmore’s2008/2011Swift and currentJBS identities do not establish the operator during his undated student job; retained employer-location description. Obtain period-specific company/employment records. Board/private practice hours and leave still unresolved.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: Australian Business Register history identifies NEUMANN & TURNOUR LAWYERS as The Ezra No 2 Unit Trust's trading name from 10 September 2007. This is operating-entity evidence only and is not converted to Neumann's appointment, payroll or cessation date. Public profiles claiming the firm was founded in 1981 conflict with his own 1983 clerkship/age-26 partnership sequence and are not used as his employment boundary. Fresh legal-admission, clerkship and Dinmore-operator searches did not resolve the remaining gaps.

Follow-up2026-10-04: targeted legal-admission, university completion, Dinmore operator, Baptist board and clerk-employer searches did not resolve boundaries, hours or leave. A reproduced2006 judgment C and C and Anor [2006] FMCAfam229 at https://casechat.au/cases/au/c-and-c-and-anor mentions an affidavit by Shayne Neumann and a Neumann Turnour2005 costs agreement; original AustLII open inaccessible. This is a corroborating practice observation, not a new appointment, cessation, personal billed-hours or weekly-workload fact, and no career field changed. Firm partner Matthew Turnour admission dates were rejected as Neumann evidence; court/firm personnel and period-specific Dinmore records remain needed.

Follow-up2026-10-05: a targeted Queensland Law Society/court-tribute search found a first-person legal-yearbook speech in which Neumann recalls appearances in Brisbane, Townsville and Lismore. Original2014 tribute and full-yearbook PDFs at https://media.sclqld.org.au/documents/publications/queensland-legal-yearbook/2014/tributes.pdf and https://archive.sclqld.org.au/sclpub/queensland-legal-yearbook/2014/queensland-legal-yearbook-2014.pdf both returned(403) Forbidden. Accessible indexed excerpt supplies neither clerk-employer identity nor dates/hours; judge admission and court service in surrounding tribute text concern the judge, not Neumann. Member/ALP and Baptist-board searches repeat known biography. CurrentQLS register names Jeanette Neumann, not Shayne; firm-wide legal-aid payments do not establish his payroll or billed hours. No employer/date/status field changed. Follow-up remains original clerk personnel, court admission/practice records and dated board appointments; no inferred full-time years.
